Submission Date: 10/30/2026

documents.text:
Kenneth Rodriguez, Maitland, FL.
Docket Number: P-15423-000
Subject: Please deny the DeepGreen project in Cook Inlet

   I am writing to ask FERC to reject the DeepGreen underwater data center project (Docket P-15423-000). Placing 350 tidal turbines and 66 subsea pods right in the middle of Cook Inlet is a terrible idea for the endangered beluga whales.
There are only about 331 of these whales left, which is a massive 75% drop from their historic numbers. They are already struggling to survive around all the shipping, oil drilling, and pollution in the area.

   Belugas depend entirely on sound to hunt, travel, and stay together in dark waters. Putting a massive, loud 100-megawatt industrial project directly in their officially designated critical habitat will ruin their ability to communicate. The noise and thermal discharge could cause hearing damage, split up whale families, and destroy their food supply.

   Losing even one more whale could push this species to extinction. FERC needs to look at the big picture and protect these animals instead of letting a company crowd them out. Please don't let this project move forward.
